messages:
kmiller: Heads up — started seeing a weird wear/anomaly pattern on local NVMe in us-west2 that is blocking ~12 GPU allocs. eviction rate spiked and janitor kicked in which in turn triggered scrub passes.

maria: can you paste the error lines? which fleet?

kmiller: gnode pool g-ux-west2-b. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-19T18:02:11Z] scrub: io_wait spike: 420ms avg over 30s, ops/s 65k -> throttle
[2026-03-19T18:02:14Z] nvme0n1: critical_warning=0x2, wear_leveling_count=87, used_pct=71
[2026-03-19T18:02:17Z] janitor: reclaim loop increased concurrency -> fsync storms
```

sanjay: hmm wear_leveling_count 87 is high for that fleet type. are the drives mixed firmware?

devon: iostat snapshot from the affected node: 
```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           12.1    0.0    6.3   34.8    0.0   46.8
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s
nvme0n1         3200.0  1800.0  204800  512000    0.0    0.0
nvme1n1          120.0    90.0    4096   16384    0.0    0.0
```

maria: that skew is wild — nvme0n1 is taking the whole workload. Is this a metadata hotspot or a physical wear-induced latency?

kmiller: initial heap: scrub + janitor overlapped with a GPU batch launch window. Janitor policy is aggressive for tempfile GC so it rebalanced many small deletes onto nvme0n1. Also our scrub sampler was scheduled across all devices at same minute.

sanjay: two quick mitigations: 1) throttle janitor concurrency on the fleet for 30m, 2) stagger scrub windows to avoid alignment. We can also pin high-throughput GPU jobs to nodes with newer drive age.

devon: agreed. opsbot can you run the quick throttle script and mark this as maintenance?

opsbot: @opsbot executing: /usr/local/bin/janitor-throttle --pool g-ux-west2-b --concurrency 2 --ttl 30m
opsbot: Maintenance ticket created: #MF-2026-1345

maria: also check SMART differences across nvme0n1 vs nvme1n1, might be firmware bug causing one controller to escalate IOs. Run: 
```
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep 'critical_warning|percentage_used|temperature'
sudo nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0n1 | grep -i firmware
```

kmiller: ran smart-log; nvme0n1 shows temp 64C, percentage_used 71, critical_warning 2. Firmware is A1. nvme1n1 is firmware A0 and pct_used 33.

sanjay: firmware mismatch + wear skew means the controller is likely doing extra background relocation on the older firmware which spikes background GC. We should favor rolling workloads off nvme0n1 until firmware is updated or the drive is retired.

devon: short-term plan I deployed: 1) reduced janitor concurrency (done), 2) scheduled staggered scrub windows (patch queued), 3) set allocation policy to avoid nvme0n1 for next 2 hours.

maria: thanks. can we quantify impact? did GPU allocs unfreeze?

kmiller: freed 9/12 allocs in ~7 minutes after throttling; remaining 3 waiting on cleaner eviction finish. iops on nvme0n1 dropped from 3200 r/s to 600 r/s.

sanjay: next steps for follow-up post-mitigation: 
- add a probe that looks for per-device coarse-grained wear skew and flags when ratio > 2x
- add firmware tag to node metadata and prefer homogeneous firmware for allocation or flag for draining
- consider cost calculus: prefer reserving a small set of prewarmed nodes with newer NVMEs for large GPU spikes (cost vs blocked time)

devon: I can open a PR for the probe. proposal: sample percent_used over 5m sliding window and emit anomaly if one device > 1.8x median.

maria: that rule sounds reasonable. also add a quick doc blurb for support runbook: what to do when janitor+scrub overlap.

kmiller: note for doc: quick commands we used to triage (copy to runbook): 
```
# live iostat
sudo iostat -x 1 10
# nvme smart
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
# force reduce janitor concurrency
/opt/redwood/tools/janitorctl set-concurrency g-ux-west2-b 2
# deprioritize device in allocator (temporary)
/opt/redwood/tools/allocator pin-avoid --device nvme0n1 --ttl 2h
```

opsbot: follow-up checklist created on #MF-2026-1345: firmware-rollout, probe-PR, runbook-update, capacity-plan

maria: moving to postmortem: capture cost tradeoff of maintaining small hot pool vs blocked GPU time. devon can you estimate cost of prewarmed nodes?

devon: will calc. rough ballpark: 5 prewarmed p4d-like nodes ~ $6k/mo vs ~ $12k/mo in lost developer/productivity if we see 4 blocked incidents/yr. will produce numbers.

sanjay: thanks everyone. tagging this resolved for now — we keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

kmiller: resolved for now. logging this in incidents repo and runbook.
